correctness.rationale: On nonzero periodic amplitudes there is no visit to the absorbing zero. Substituting the two branches gives logistic amplitude and an independent action on sign (identity for -a, transposition for +a). Sign return requires a multiple of the amplitude period and, for +a, an even time. This gives the least periods and number of lifts, with zero counted separately. At odd n the positive-parameter fixed count is 1; at even n both counts are 2P_n-1. Taking formal logarithms gives the stated zeta products; the correction in the positive case has coefficient -(-1)^n/n. The full-tent conjugacy at a=4 gives an intersection with the diagonal in every one of the 2^n monotone full branches, and no duplicate periodic point at shared branch boundaries. This gives both rational zetas. The transfer operator averages over one inverse point per dyadic subinterval; the averages converge uniformly for continuous densities and in L1 for all densities by contraction and approximation. All powers have the unique arcsine ACIP after conjugacy and are mixing. The sign actions give two mixing ergodic ACIPs and their mixtures at -4, versus equal sign weights and the unique square-invariant conditional densities at +4. The latter measure is ergodic because the square is ergodic on each half and the halves exchange; its sign correlation is (-1)^n. The exchange is a mod-null statement, since endpoints mapping to zero do not literally swap. Entropy is log 2 by the invariant-half conjugacies (for the square in the positive case) and the iteration identity.
residual_risks: Exact finite replay covers the endpoint only; the formal all-parameter result and the measure conclusions follow analytically. Nothing claims uniqueness among singular measures or any mixing classification away from a=4.
